2-3-1-economic-growth-and-the-economic-c.title: Economic Growth and the Economic Cycle

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows the aggregate demand (AD) and long-run aggregate supply (LRAS) curves for an economy. All other things being equal, which one of the following is most likely to cause aggregate demand to shift from AD1 to AD2 and long-run aggregate supply to shift from LRAS1 to LRAS2?
options: A fall in spending on imports and a rise in productivity
A reduction in exports and an increase in imports of capital goods
An increase in Bank Rate and a reduction in firms’ costs of production
An increase in saving and a rise in government spending on infrastructure

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the most likely reason for a fall in saving by households?
options: A reduction in consumer confidence
A reduction in income tax rates
An increase in household energy bills
An increase in interest rates

questions.questionText: According to the accelerator process
options: a fall in the price of capital goods encourages more investment.
an increase in investment leads to a greater increase in national income.
firms invest to increase spare capacity.
investment is determined by past changes in national income.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to cause a rightward shift in an aggregate demand curve? An increase in
options: indirect taxation.
interest rates.
international competitiveness.
the budget surplus.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following best explains the operation of the accelerator process?
options: An increase in investment leads to a larger increase in national income
An increase in productive capacity leads to a larger change in investment
The growth of productive capacity depends on the growth in investment
The level of investment depends on the rate of change in national income

questions.questionText: An aggregate demand and short-run aggregate supply diagram is used to illustrate the effect of a rise in imports of goods and services into an economy. All other things being equal, which one of the following would be shown on the diagram?
options: A leftward movement along the aggregate demand curve
A leftward movement along the short-run aggregate supply curve
A rightward shift of the aggregate demand curve
A rightward shift of the short-run aggregate supply curve

questions.questionText: Which one of the following explains the operation of the accelerator process in an economy?
options: Increasing investment leads to a rise in aggregate demand
National income increases as a result of rising investment
National income rises as a result of an increase in aggregate demand
Rising national income leads to an increase in investment

questions.questionText: A government decides to increase the minimum wage at a time when the rest of the world is coming out of recession. These events cause short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) to shift from SRAS1 to SRAS2 and aggregate demand (AD) to shift from AD1 to AD2. If the initial macroeconomic equilibrium is E1, which one of the following diagrams shows the correct new equilibrium E2?
Table 2 shows the components of a country’s national income in 2021. It can be concluded from the data in Table 2 that aggregate supply in 2021 must have been
Which one of the following is most likely to result in an increase in exports from the UK economy? An increase in
options: inflation in other countries.
productivity in other countries.
UK incomes.
UK interest rates.

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows the aggregate demand (AD) and short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) curves for an economy. Which one of the following combinations of events is most likely to cause the curves to shift from AD1 to AD2 and from SRAS1 to SRAS2?
options: A higher rate of savings and faster labour productivity growth
Faster economic growth abroad and lower world commodity prices
Higher money wages and more household consumption
Lower interest rates and a higher rate of indirect taxes

questions.questionText: Faster growth in national income caused investment in an economy to increase. This means that the increase in investment resulted from
options: an increase in spare capacity.
lower interest rates.
the action of the accelerator.
the action of the multiplier.

questions.questionText: Table 2 shows the components of aggregate demand in an economy which is in equilibrium. If imports increase to £230 billion and the multiplier is 1.5, then the new level of national income would be
options: £1155 billion
£1455 billion
£1545 billion
£1845 billion

questions.questionText: Explain the main causes of rising consumption in an economy.
To what extent do you agree that a fall in savings is beneficial for the UK economy? Justify your answer.

Figure 4 shows two aggregate demand (AD1 and AD2) curves and two long-run aggregate supply (LRAS1 and LRAS2) curves for an economy. All other things being equal, which one of the following is the most likely explanation for the movement of the economy from E1 to E2?
options: A decline in the capital stock resulting from a significant decline in bank funding for business investment
An increase in net foreign investment by firms following a reduction in the rate of inflation
An unexpected reduction in the rate of interest following a fall in the rate of inflation
The growth of government borrowing to fund increased expenditure on infrastructure

questions.questionText: According to the accelerator process, a slowdown in the rate of growth of national income will lead to a fall in the
options: level of investment.
marginal propensity to save.
rate of interest.
value of the multiplier.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following combinations of possible shocks: A, B, C, or D, is most likely to move an economy from a negative output gap to a positive output gap? An unexpected increase in
options: productivity growth combined with a larger than expected decrease in inflation.
the exchange rate combined with an unexpected fall in business confidence.
the government’s budget surplus combined with a downturn in world trade.
the marginal propensity to consume combined with a fall in the exchange rate.

questions.questionText: Figure 10 shows two aggregate demand (AD1 and AD2) curves and two short-run aggregate supply (SRAS1 and SRAS2) curves for an economy. All other things being equal, which one of the following is the most likely explanation for the movement of the economy from E1 to E2?
options: A depreciation of the currency and an increase in interest rates
A fall in the prices of raw materials and an increase in investment
An increase in exports and the rate of Value Added Tax
An increase in the supply of money and the level of money wages

questions.questionText: Figure 7 shows two aggregate demand (AD1 and AD2) curves and two long-run aggregate supply (LRAS1 and LRAS2) curves for an economy. All other things being equal, which one of the following combinations, A, B, C or D, is most likely to explain the movement of the economy from E1 to E2? An increase in the
options: budget surplus and size of the multiplier.
exchange rate and supply of money.
rate of inflation and positive output gap.
volume of exports and potential output.

questions.questionText: The quantity of food imported by an economy increases by 12% in one year. The most likely cause is a fall in
options: domestic farm prices.
income tax.
the exchange rate.
welfare benefits.

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows aggregate demand (AD) curves for an economy. Which one of the following is most likely to cause the aggregate demand curve to shift from AD1 to AD2?
options: A fall in imports
A fall in the price level
A reduction in the budget deficit
A rise in the exchange rate

questions.questionText: Figure 2 shows the aggregate demand (AD) curves and short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) curves for an economy. Which one of the following combinations of events is most likely to cause aggregate demand to shift from AD1 to AD2 and short-run aggregate supply from SRAS1 to SRAS2?
options: A fall in income tax and lower raw material prices
A fall in net exports and higher labour productivity
A rise in money wages and a rise in household saving
An increase in VAT and a rise in household wealth

questions.questionText: Many firms use profits to finance their capital investment instead of borrowing from banks. For these firms, higher interest rates are most likely to
options: cause them to change the type of investment made with more investment in buildings.
cause them to reduce their investment as they can now earn more interest from saving their profits.
have no impact on the amount of investment undertaken as they pay no interest.
result in more investment as they can earn more interest on money deposited in banks.

questions.questionText: There is a large depreciation in an economy’s exchange rate but the value of its exports does not increase. The most likely reason for the absence of an increase in the value of exports is that
options: consumer confidence in the economy has fallen.
other countries are in recession.
the government has implemented contractionary fiscal policy.
there is an increase in unemployment in the economy.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand curves (AD) and short-run aggregate supply curves (SRAS) for an economy. Which one of the following combinations of events is most likely to have caused the shift from AD1 to AD2 and the shift from SRAS1 to SRAS2?
options: A fall in commodity prices and a fall in savings
A fall in money wages and an increase in imports
An increase in the budget deficit and a fall in productivity
An increase in VAT and an increase in income tax

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the aggregate demand curve (AD), short-run aggregate supply curve (SRAS), and long-run aggregate supply curve (LRAS) for an economy. The current level of real GDP is Y. Which one of the following policies is most likely, in the short run, to bring the economy closer to its normal capacity level of output?
options: An increase in the target rate of inflation
Higher government spending on vocational education
Lower rates of tax on manufacturing businesses
New schemes to encourage more household saving

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the actual level of real GDP and the trend level of real GDP over time for an economy. The economy starts its recovery from recession at point M. After several years of growth the economy reaches point N. All other things being equal, which one of the following is the most likely consequence of the economy’s growth path between points M and N?
options: A decrease in the level of interest rates due to deflation.
A decrease in the rate of inflation due to increased output.
An increase in investment due to the accelerator process.
An increase in the value of the multiplier due to a rise in the savings ratio.

questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract D (Figure 4), calculate the average amount saved per household in 2016 if average household income was £26 300. Give your answer to the nearest pound.
Europe and North America enter a period of recovery from a recession. Other things remaining the same, the impact on the UK economy is most likely to be
options: an increase in structural unemployment.
an increase in the current account deficit.
a reduction in cyclical unemployment.
a reduction in UK economic growth.

questions.questionText: Explain how the data in Extract D (Figures 3 and 4) show that consumer confidence may have risen since 2014.
Which one of the following best describes the action of the accelerator theory of investment?
options: Firms decide to invest more following a cut in bank rate
Firms invest in capital equipment due to higher economic growth
Improved business confidence causes firms to increase their investment
Large profits encourage firms to invest in new capital equipment

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the best definition of a household’s total saving?
options: An injection into the circular flow of income
Contributions to a pension fund for retirement
Money placed in bank and building society accounts
That part of disposable income not spent on consumption

questions.questionText: In the diagram below, an economy is initially in equilibrium at point G. Aggregate demand then shifts from AD1 to AD2 and the short-run aggregate supply curve shifts from SRAS1 to SRAS2. Which one of the following combinations of events will cause these shifts in AD and SRAS and move the economy to a new equilibrium at point H?
options: A cut in income tax and an increase in VAT
A fall in money wages and a fall in house prices
An increase in productivity and a rise in consumer confidence
Higher energy prices and lower government expenditure

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows two aggregate demand (AD) curves and the short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) curve for an economy. All other things being equal, the change in real national output from Y1 to Y2 is most likely to have been caused by an increase in the
options: government’s budget deficit.
level of interest rates.
size of the labour force.
volume of exports.

questions.questionText: The diagrams below show the aggregate demand (AD) and short run aggregate supply (SRAS) curves for an economy. AD1 and SRAS1 show the initial positions of the curves and AD2 and SRAS2 the new positions. Which one of the following diagrams, A, B, C or D, illustrates a fall in world commodity prices as well as a fall in government spending?
The table below shows the components of gross domestic product (GDP) for an economy in 2016. Aggregate demand in the economy is
Which one of the following represents investment expenditure?
options: A firm spends £7m on new computer software
A government spends £10m more on nurses wages
A household puts £10 000 into an interest paying account
An individual spends £28 000 buying company shares

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to reduce cyclical unemployment in the UK?
options: A cut in the UK budget deficit
An increase in the pound sterling exchange rate
An increase in the UK retirement age
Higher economic growth in the Eurozone

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows two aggregate demand curves (AD) for an economy. All other things being equal, the most likely cause of the shift from AD1 to AD2 is an increase in
options: exports.
the rate of inflation.
interest rates.
the budget deficit.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows two aggregate demand curves (AD) and the short-run aggregate supply curve (SRAS) for an economy. All other things being equal, which one of the following is the most likely cause of the movement of the economy from equilibrium at Y1 to equilibrium at Y2?
options: A decrease in imports
An increase in savings
A decrease in the money supply
An increase in productivity
